core_principles.text: Adjusting hand and wrist positions during push-ups can selectively activate the serratus anterior to target scapular stability.
Lateral hand placement can be utilized during push-ups to maximize the activation of the serratus anterior muscle.

specific_findings.text: In a study of 31 healthy young male participants (23.65 ± 0.49 years), hand position had a significant effect on serratus anterior activation (p < 0.001, η2 = 0.215), with lateral hand placement exhibiting the greatest activation.
Hand position significantly affected lower trapezius (p = 0.01, η2 = 0.088), upper trapezius (p = 0.002, η2 = 0.13), and biceps brachii (p = 0.003, η2 = 0.132) activation during push-ups.
No significant differences in muscle activation were found in the triceps brachii and pectoralis major across the tested hand and wrist positions.
